summary: Ronald M. Davidson is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He earned his PhD from the University of California, Berkeley in 1985, and held posts as Professor at California State University, Northridge and at Fairfield University.

Ronald Merry Macphail (1899–1974) was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He studied at The Glasgow Academy and the University of Glasgow, later serving with the Church of Scotland (1925) and at the Bamdah Medical Mission (circa 1927–1967).

Ronald Morton Smith (1916–1999) was an Indologist who studied at St Andrews, Oxford, and Cambridge. He served as Lecturer in Sanskrit at Cambridge (1948–1955), Assistant Professor at the University of Toronto (1955–1982), and chairman at Harvard (1976–1978).

Ronald Neufeldt (born 1941) is a religious studies and Indology scholar. His career was based at the University of Calgary, where he served as Associate Professor (circa 1981–1989), faculty member until circa 2006, and subsequently Professor Emeritus.

Ronald S. Green works in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. Educated at UNC Charlotte, Virginia Tech, Oregon, and Wisconsin-Madison, he held positions at Wisconsin-Madison, Coastal Carolina University (attested 2013), and ASIANetwork (2020–2025).

Ronald Y. Nakasone (born 1943) is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 1980. He held academic posts at the Institute of Buddhist Studies (circa 1988) and the Pacific School of Religion (attested 1996).

Rong Geng (1894–1983) was a scholar in Sinology, history, archaeology, and linguistics. He studied at Peking University from circa 1922 to 1925 and later held a post at Yenching University from circa 1926 to 1941.

Rongdao Lai specializes in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Sinology. Supervised by G. Victor Sōgen Hori and Robin D. S. Yates, she earned her PhD from McGill University, later holding posts at the Center for Chinese Studies and McGill.

Ronit Ricci (born 1966) works in Indology, religious studies, and linguistics. She studied at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem (circa 1989–1993) and held posts at the Australian National University in 2010 and the Hebrew University of Jerusalem in 2014.

Ronit Yoeli-Tlalim is a scholar of history, archaeology, Tibetology, and Sinology. She completed her PhD at SOAS University of London (1998–2004) and held posts at University College London (attested 2010) and Goldsmiths, University of London (2023–2024).

Roper Lethbridge (1840–1919) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Exeter College (circa 1859–1863), served in the Indian Civil Service (circa 1868–1878), and was a Fellow of the University of Calcutta.
Rory Brendan Lindsay is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Toronto and completed his PhD at Harvard University under Leonard van der Kuijp.
Rory Mackenzie specializes in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He completed his doctoral studies under Peter Harvey and served as a teacher at International Christian College.

Rosalind Lefeber is an Indologist who completed her doctoral dissertation at the University of Toronto under supervisors Bimal Krishna Matilal and Ronald Morton Smith. She held a post at the University of Toronto (attested 2007).

Rosalind O'Hanlon works in Indology and history. She earned her PhD from SOAS University of London (circa 1978–1983) and held appointments at Clare College (circa 1989–2006), the University of Oxford (circa 2006–2020), and the British Academy (2020).

Rosan Ikeda (born 1941) is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied and taught at Komazawa University from 1960 to 2012, serving as a professor from 1983 to 2012. In 2009, he served as director at the Soto Zen Research Center.

Rosane Rocher (born 1937) is an Indologist and linguist who studied under Ludo Rocher at Université libre de Bruxelles. She held posts at the National Fund for Scientific Research, the University of Pennsylvania (from 1970), and the Rocher Foundation.

Rosemarie Fuchs (born 1950) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She studied under Katia Holmes and Khenpo Tsultrim Gyamtso Rinpoche, and served as a member of the Marpa Translation Committee (attested 2000).

Rosemarie Lühr (born 1946) is a linguist and Indologist who earned her doctorate under Karl Hoffmann at Erlangen-Nuremberg. She held professorships at the universities of Giessen, Jena, and Humboldt Berlin, and was president of the Indogermanische Gesellschaft (2004–2016).

Rosemary Radford Ruether (1936–2022) was a religious studies scholar. She completed her studies at the Claremont School of Theology (circa 1960–1965) and held an academic post at Howard University from circa 1965 to 1975.
